Phainon swirled his drink leisurely between his fingers.

He hated these meetings - yet with his line of shady yet boring work in this world he was doomed to attend them. 

Doomed to sit there and have their stupid ‘rabbits’ brushing against him, rubbing on him, trying their best to entice him. Trying their best to win a better deal for their business owner, doing everything they could with hands trailing up his slacks - up his thighs.

It was all so very boring.

Those ‘bunnies’ were never his type.

He didn’t even know what his type was, to be honest, but he did know they weren’t it.

Most humans weren’t, and none that he had ever met was.

“Has your company considered our proposition well, Mr. Khaslana?” 

Those words drew his eyes again - languidly rising to meet with the golden hair woman’s own. 

They had done this so, so, many times.

Everytime it was the same dance that he was becoming an expert in.

It was tiring. 

“Our exports are doing quite well this year,” Phainon paused, eyes dragging over the fake golden cup in his hand to stare at the red liquid in it in the dim lighting - the thumming of the bass of the song below the VIP room was beyond annoying in his skull by now. “Wouldn’t you agree?”

Phainon flitted his eyes back to the woman across the table, sitting properly, eyes only staring him down with a small smile on her painted lips - a lie.

The smile was a lie, it always was, no one was ever happy to see Phainon appear at their establishment. He was no better than a loan shark, and considering his diet and his sharpened teeth - he practically was a shark smelling bloodied waters. 

“You’re saying you will continue to not agree with the deal, correct?” 

Phainon’s eyes drifted to the drink again, swaying it in his hands with a heavy exhale - watching the liquid splash slightly over the rim and down the side, trailing against his fingers. Not that he minded. He was never going to drink it regardless, he needed a clear mind for these types of meetings. Especially considering how smart this specific woman was. 

Phainon couldn’t help the laugh that fluttered out of his lips as he tilted that drink just a bit more wastefully, watching it drip onto the floor, watching those play bunnies scramble to clean it up. Or perhaps lick at the drops before it was hitting the floor. He wasn’t sure.

He didn’t care.

His icy piercing eyes found their way back once again to Aglaea - bored as he blinked at her.

“To be frank, You’ve never shown me anything or anyone worth investing into.” Phainon told her with a small smile, one that had all the malice in his heart laced into it. 

It wasn’t her fault.

Aglaea was someone he actually quite respected, these ‘bunnies’ were another issue. Escorts that were dull, mundane, and didn’t catch his eye. 

How was he supposed to invest in her when none of them even made him blink twice? 

Never made his breath stutter?

Never made his heart rate rise even a little?

How was he supposed to care about some humans here?

He wasn’t even exactly human himself, and the idea of caring about humans that weren’t even impressive.. Well.

He huffed out a quiet scoff over his own thoughts.

“My apologies. Do you have any idea what you specifically would like to see during these meetings?” Aglaea inquired, her head tilting and that was a curious question.

He didn’t know.

He had never found someone that caught his eye - escort or not. 

Stripper or not. 

Upstanding citizen or not.

All humans were the same to him.

A meal.

Crunchy and delicious to eat, even if his kind did breed with them - until he met the one he desired as a mate for the rest of his life and bonded with them, they were just meals to him. 

There were no simple answers he could give her.

“I wonder that too, Aglaea.” Phainon boredly muttered out, moving to put that half empty cup on the table messily - watching the liquid still trickle down the side of it with such a deep sigh. One that made him crease his brows as his eyes flitted to the glass window that overlooked the rest of the ‘establishment’. 

The club that had a steady heartbeat of life as its pulse constantly.

Dining.. Escorts.. Strippers.. Such a shady place, such a good line of work for a creature from the abyss like himself. 

A creature that people said were only real in fairy tales and horror shows - but he was so very real. And meals were easy to come by in a world like this where no one batted an eye when one of them went missing. 

Perfect for a monster like himself, dragging people away to never be seen again - never to have their bodies found. Crunched beneath his own appendages and chewed into bits and pieces to be swallowed.

There was no flavor.

There was nothing of interest. 

“Mr. Khaslana, You forgot your order to go.” 

Those words were spoken so dryly, and with a hand gently touching Phainon’s shoulder for his attention that the next few seconds seemed like a blur.

An absolute chaotic mess as Phainon only heard the immediate shattering of a plate or glass behind him as his bodyguards moved into position at a threatening pace. Snapping into their role and duty at the drop of a pen, Phainon only gave a sideways glance over his shoulder.
